sentence: This project studies how genes, gene activity and health record features overlap in bipolar disorder and schizophrenia.
This project tries to find out how a molecule turns pericytes into muscle-like cells that narrow lung blood vessels through the protein vimentin.
This project builds a database that links pathology, radiology imaging and clinical information for prostate cancer research.
This project studies how mutated forms of a protein that controls DNA in our genome cause an inherited small vessel disease of the brain.
This project studies how predatory bacteria and their prey interact in a host microbiome and how this predation affects the host.
This project studies how an enzyme that modifies RNA helps cancer stem cells grow in glioblastoma.
This project studies how a protein controls hemoglobin genes in red blood cells and how that protein is itself controlled during development.
This project studies how a retinoid-related protein affects intestinal endocrine cells and the hormones they make.
This project studies how a protein called lipocalin-2 helps solid tumors spread and survive.
This project studies which cell processes protect retinal ganglion cells and help their axons regrow in eye diseases such as glaucoma.
This project studies how dental pulp stem cells form and keep neurovascular stem cell niches when used for tissue regeneration.
This project studies the genes behind parthenogenesis, which is reproduction without sex, in the freshwater microcrustacean Daphnia.
This project builds a platform that finds antibiotics by growing previously uncultured bacteria and screening single cells in microdroplets.
This project tries to find out how switching tumor suppressor genes back on could help treat acute myeloid leukemia.
This project studies how chronic stress changes gene activity in the hippocampal–prefrontal pathway and whether this causes fear and anxiety.
This project aims to bridge the gap between basic scientific research and its use in clinical practice.
This project builds gene expression and mutation datasets and better gene knockout methods for the ciliate Tetrahymena.
This project tries to find out what causes smell, brain and thinking problems that last after COVID-19 infection, using a mouse model.
This project tests whether self-sampling tools help patients who are behind on screening complete screening for colorectal cancer and cervical cancer.
This project uses umbilical cord stem cells to study how fat and muscle cells develop and work in Klinefelter syndrome.
